transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-20 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Jonas Li (Redwood SE); Sara Nguyen (BrightSide - Head of ML); Carlos Mendes (BrightSide CTO); Priya Rao (BrightSide SRE); Liam O'Connor (Product)

Summary: finalizing canary and cutover plan, monitoring/runbooks, rollback windows, A/B gating and timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda - canary plan, monitoring & runbooks, rollback criteria, and timelines. we have 45 minutes so we'll try to keep it tight. Sara, Carlos, you good with that?
[00:12] Sara: yep, sounds good. thanks Maya. excited to get this in motion.
[00:16] Carlos: yes, quick heads up - we want minimal risk to core payments flow, that's the hard stop.
[00:23] Jonas: understood. we'll scope canary to non-payments traffic first and pick a small percentage, run it behind a feature flag, and then expand if metrics look stable.
[00:34] Priya: can you confirm where the canary will run - hosted Redwood or our dedicated instance? we need to know network paths for monitoring.
[00:42] Maya: good question. plan is to run the canary on Redwood Dedicated reserved pool in us-west-2 - that mirrors expected perf. but we can also do an initial functional canary on hosted if you prefer. Jonas, maybe clarify differences?
[00:54] Jonas: yeah, hosted will be faster to stand up but dedicated gives us the same GPU topology and quantization profile you'll run in prod. for perf and latency SLO validation we strongly recommend dedicated for the production canary.
[01:06] Sara: ok, dedicated makes sense. what's your recommendation on canary size? 1%, 2%, 5%?
[01:13] Jonas: recommend 2% for 24 hours as a first pass. that gives enough requests to validate tail latency and cost signal without exposing too many users. if we see no regressions we can step to 10% during a second window.
[01:27] Carlos: and what metrics will we use to decide go/no-go?
[01:31] Maya: agreed criteria - latency P99 within 15% of baseline, error rate below 0.1% delta, cost per 1k tokens within expected band, and model output quality checks via sampled prompt set. Priya, does that align with your on-call thresholds?
[01:46] Priya: yes, P99 is the big one for us. we also want an alert if CPU or GPU memory starts trending up beyond 70% for more than 5 minutes. and a runbook step to automatically cut traffic if errors spike.
[01:58] Jonas: we'll add automated webhooks to your pager duty via the Redwood console. we can instrument token-level latency and queue wait time too so you can see batching effects.
[02:09] Liam: quick question on A/B testing - can we route 50% of a subset of sessions to the new model variant while keeping the rest on legacy? we want a qualitative comparison.
[02:19] Jonas: yes, Redwood supports per-route A/B routing. for the pilot I'd suggest just a small user cohort - maybe 1k sessions - otherwise the signal gets noisy. also we'll capture side-by-side outputs and diff metrics.
[02:32] Sara: on quality checks, can we run automated evals against our labeled prompt set? last week we ran an offline eval and saw a slight regression on technical terms.
[02:41] Maya: absolutely - we'll integrate your eval suite into the canary. Jonas will run a nightly eval during the 24 hour canary and share results.
[02:49] Carlos: what about fallback - if the model degrades, do we auto-fallback to the previous model or to a cheaper variant? what's typical?
[02:58] Jonas: configurable. common pattern is fallback to a smaller compatible variant that has similar tokenizer/outputs or to the previous stable model. for latency-sensitive routes some customers prefer immediate fallback; others prefer throttling. we'll align on policy.
[03:11] Priya: we need explicit rollback criteria in the runbook - who triggers rollback, and is it manual or automated?
[03:18] Maya: good point. proposal: automatic traffic cut to 0% if error rate above threshold for 5 mins, but human-approved rollback for model changes that fail quality checks. we'll document owners and escalation steps.
[03:29] Sara: can Jonas draft that in the runbook with clear owners?
[03:32] Jonas: yes, I'll add the automated thresholds, manual rollback steps, and who to call (Maya, Jonas, Sara, Priya).
[03:39] Maya: ok. monitoring - what dashboards do you want?
[03:43] Priya: token-level latency, P50/P90/P99, request queue length, GPU utilization, memory, error codes, and a small sample of model outputs. also an incidents log in the Redwood console and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[03:58] Jonas: we can ship a dashboard template and enable audit log forwarding to your Kinesis stream. note that some product names in our console might appear as "Red wood" in transcription exports, but it's the Redwood console.
[04:12] Carlos: security questions - SOC2 compliance and KMS key handling. will logs contain PII? we need assurance about redaction and retention.
[04:21] Maya: yes, Redwood is SOC2 and we'll share the security pack. by default we do not persist full user payloads in logs - we can enable redaction and customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest. Jonas, follow up on retention defaults?
[04:33] Jonas: default retention 30 days for detailed traces; we can extend retention for audit logs on request. and we support customer-provided KMS for the private deployment.
[04:42] Sara: great - please send the security pack again. we did not fully review last week.
[04:46] Maya: will do. action items will capture that.
[04:49] Liam: timeline wise, when would you like to run the canary?
[04:53] Jonas: propose week of 2026-05-27 for a dry-run and production canary the week after, with cutover target 2026-06-03 in the 02:00 PT window to minimize user impact.
[05:05] Carlos: that window looks fine pending Priya's on-call schedule.
[05:09] Priya: i'll check and confirm by Monday. i also need a quick dry-run to validate our alert hooks.
[05:17] Sara: we also want to share our top 10 critical queries, and a list of scheduled marketing pushes that might create traffic spikes. i'll send that.
[05:24] Maya: thanks - so to recap: Redwood to produce canary runbook + config (Jonas) by 2026-05-22; dry-run week of 2026-05-27; production canary 2% for 24 hrs then evaluate; cutover target 2026-06-03; customer to provide traffic calendar and confirm on-call windows.
[05:40] Carlos: one last thing - cost monitoring. we need to understand unit economics during the canary, and if we plan to move to dedicated we need committed cost numbers.
[05:49] Maya: i'll send an updated pricing note, and we can model cost per 1k tokens during the canary. if you decide to reserve capacity we'll share committed pricing options.
[05:58] Sara: perfect. thanks everyone.
[06:01] Maya: thanks all - we'll follow up in email and share the runbook. meeting adjourned.

References and links mentioned: Redwood canary runbook (to be shared), security pack (SOC2), demo recording link (internal), sample eval spreadsheet (Sara to share).
